audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers agree on Skill / Skill / Skill / Vladimir / Skill / Skill / Vladimir, but the first three whys all describe Trundle winning outright — "he has no escape and no answer to the first trade", "you can run him down after any trade he tries to walk away from", "stack three Chomps before his Q sustain can offset the damage" — and `early` says "short trades are yours every time" and "you can freely run him down".
audit.why: Levels 1 to 3 are not a coin flip here and the page already knows it. Sanguine Pool is 28 seconds at rank 1, which is far too expensive to spend on poke, and Transfusion at 9 seconds costs him no mana but heals only what one cast heals. Trundle at 51.36% over 294 games is an even lane overall, and the way that arithmetic actually works is a Trundle-favoured start against a Vladimir-favoured scale.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 2 and 3 to Trundle in both layers; 4-5 and 2+ items stay Vladimir's; level 6 and first item stay Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hemoplague is absent from the content layer entirely, and Crimson Rush is never mentioned. `spikes[3]` describes his late game as "kills you in one rotation" with no cue for when the rotation starts.
audit.why: Hemoplague is a 120-second, 625-range zone that makes affected enemies take INCREASED DAMAGE for its duration before it detonates and heals him per champion hit. It is not the damage that kills you, it is the amplification on everything after it — which makes his ultimate the cue to leave, and its 120 seconds exactly as long as your Subjugate. Crimson Rush is the other missing tell: Riot's text says Transfusion gets massively increased damage and healing when his resource bar is full, so a full bar is a loaded Q.
audit.corrected: Hemoplague: 120s, amplifies all damage you take for its duration, then heals him per champion hit. A full Crimson Rush bar is a loaded Transfusion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five separate fields describe a Subjugate "second cast": spikes[1] "use the second cast the instant the pool ends", wants.you[1] "Land Subjugate's first cast", wants.foe[0] "Pool your Subjugate second-cast", `mid` "If he pools the second Subjugate cast", whys[4] "even if he pools the second cast".
audit.why: Subjugate has no second cast. It is one cast: it steals immediately, and Riot's text says the amount stolen doubles over the following 4 seconds. The invented mechanic produces genuinely bad play — a Trundle holding a phantom second button through Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds is a Trundle who never presses R at all, when the correct instruction is to land it before the pool and let the doubling run regardless.
audit.corrected: One cast. It steals on impact and the amount doubles over the next 4 seconds — land it before he pools.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is never named, and the one property of it that changes how Trundle stands in lane is nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's own description says the released blood "can be blocked by enemy units". Against a champion whose poke is otherwise unavoidable, keeping the minion wave between the two of you is a free defence, and it costs Vladimir his own health to charge each cast. It is 13/11/9/7/5 seconds, so at rank 5 it is nearly as frequent as Chomp.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood (13/11/9/7/5s) costs him health and Riot's text says enemy units can block it — keep the wave between you.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] says "Chomp's AS steal", `mid` says "Chomp twice for the AS steal and AD drain", and `mid` also says he will "pool every Pillar you throw to deny the knockup".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage — there is no attack-speed component, and against an AP Vladimir the sap is close to worthless anyway, which is a more useful thing to know than a stat that does not exist. Pillar of Ice has no knock-up either; it makes terrain and slows, so what the pool actually dodges is the slow and the follow-up, not a displacement.
audit.corrected: Chomp: damage, movement slow, AD sap. Pillar of Ice: terrain plus a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names no cooldown at all — packet defect "never names any of Vladimir's abilities" is confirmed for that layer — and breakdown.cooldowns gives Sanguine Pool no figure.
audit.why: The numbers are the whole plan: Sanguine Pool 28/25/22/19/16s against Pillar of Ice 21s at rank 1, Transfusion 9 down to 4.6s and free to cast, Tides of Blood 13 down to 5s, Hemoplague 120s against Subjugate's 120s. A 28-second pool is the reason levels 1 to 3 are Trundle's; a 16-second pool late is the reason they stop being.
audit.corrected: Figures added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], spikes[0], early and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] correctly buys Executioner's Calling on first back, but the content layer never mentions anti-heal once, and wants.you[2] tells you to force the level-6 all-in with no mention of it.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal against Transfusion and Hemoplague, and Riftmaker adds omnivamp on top. Three separate healing sources means Grievous Wounds has to be on him before the all-in starts, not bought after the lane has already gone wrong.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds applied before the level-6 commit; Transfusion, Hemoplague and Riftmaker all heal him.

audit.why: No suspectNames were raised for this matchup and I found no misspelled ability names — the content layer simply never uses any. Crimson Pact is worth one extra note: it converts bonus health into AP and back, so every health item he buys makes him a bigger Subjugate target rather than a safer one.

edits.before: Short trades are yours every time — one Chomp steals his Attack Damage and heals you off the dying minions his Q is trying to farm. Step up as he goes for a last-hit, land Chomp, and back off before his Q poke cooldown resets. Do not burn Pillar chasing him to his tower; save it to cut off his retreat when he tries to walk away after a losing trade. His W pool is on a long cooldown at this level and he will not waste it early, so you can freely run him down inside Frozen Domain through the first three levels without fear of the dodge.
edits.after: Short trades are yours every time — one Chomp saps his Attack Damage and King's Tribute heals you off the minions Transfusion is trying to farm. Step up as he last-hits, bite, and leave before Transfusion is back: it costs him no mana and it is 9s at rank 1. Keep the wave between the two of you where you can, because Riot's text says Tides of Blood can be blocked by enemy units. Do not burn Pillar chasing him to tower; save it to cut the walk home after a losing trade. Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1, so he will not spend it on poke and these levels are free.

edits.before: Once he has his full three-point combo (Q sustain plus the pool available) the lane becomes a management game. He will pool every Pillar you throw to deny the knockup, so bait it — walk at him as if you are committing, wait for the pool to come out, then hard-engage the moment he re-surfaces and his W is on cooldown. At level 6 go immediately: drop Frozen Domain under him, Chomp twice for the AS steal and AD drain, then hit Subjugate first-cast to take his MR. If he pools the second Subjugate cast, that is fine — you already banked half his resistances. Chase with Pillar when the pool drops.
edits.after: Once Transfusion and the pool are both online the lane becomes a management game. He will pool your Pillar of Ice to sit out the slow, so bait it — walk at him as if you are committing, wait for the two untargetable seconds, then hard-engage as he resurfaces with a 28-second cooldown behind him. At level 6 go immediately: Frozen Domain under him, Chomp twice for the AD sap, then Subjugate — one cast, and the steal doubles over the next 4 seconds, so a pool afterwards saves him nothing. His answer is Hemoplague at 120s, and it amplifies everything that lands on you.

edits.before: You are a 51-percent lane, not a stomper, and Vladimir's Rabadon's window makes that clear. By the time he has two AP items he kites outside Frozen Domain range, pools your Subjugate setup every fight, and one-rotates you before your healing scales with the damage incoming. Play the mid-game lead into objectives — force Rift Herald, take towers, and convert the lane advantage into a team fight where your Subjugate on their AP threat still warps the fight. In a straight 1v1 at thirty minutes, you lose unless you hit Pillar cold before he reacts.
edits.after: You are a 51-percent lane, not a stomper, and Vladimir's Rabadon's window makes that clear. With two AP items he kites outside Frozen Domain, pools your engage on a 16-second cooldown, and opens with Hemoplague so the rotation behind it lands amplified. Play the mid-game lead into objectives — force Rift Herald, take towers, convert the lane into a team fight where Subjugate on their AP threat still warps everything; Crimson Pact means his health items feed your R's max-health damage. In a straight 1v1 at thirty minutes you lose unless the Pillar lands cold.

notes: The invented "Subjugate second cast" appears five times in this one matchup and is the most consequential error I found on the page — it teaches a Trundle to hold his ultimate through Sanguine Pool waiting for a button that does not exist. Worth grepping every champion's file for 'second cast' near Subjugate. Also templated and wrong across this file: 'Chomp's AS steal' (it saps Attack Damage) and 'Pillar ... knockup' (terrain plus slow, no displacement) — both appear in the Urgot entry too. Crimson Pact is a genuine argument the page never makes: every point of bonus health Vladimir buys converts to AP and back, so a health-stacking Vladimir is a bigger Subjugate payout, not a safer target.
